minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 26, 2024
  CITY HALL, MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  9:30 A.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Holland called the meeting t0 order at 9:36 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Julia Holland; Commissioners Commissioner Lotte Cherin, Barry
  Haldeman, and Peter Jones

  ABSENT: Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; and Brittany Saleaumua,
  Administrative Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Commissioner Cherin seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the meeting agenda was properly posted on
  November 22, 2024.

ITEM 1.  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  l.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops were
  completed at Malibu Middle School, Webster Elementary School, and
  Distance Leaming classes. She stated a Poetry Slam event would be held on

  December 9, 2024, at Webster Elementary School, and poetry workshops
  would occur at Malibu High School in January 2025.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Vice Chair Holland stated the opening reception of Feminine Perspectives:
  A Still Life Exhibit was on November 17, 2024, and the artwork would be
  displayed through January 2025.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated he was discussing the Malibu Nights event
  with the Chamber of Commerce.

  4.  Social Media

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated artists from Feminine
  Perspectives: A Still Life Exhibit were featured on social media through a
  “Meet Our Artists” campaign. She stated the social media
  posts included
  biographies, artwork, and an artist's headshot.

  Vice Chair Holland recommended Commissioners continue sharing event
  flyers through personal social media accounts and email blasts.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Vice Chair Holland stated a booth
  at the Farmer’s Market would not be worthwhile because it required staff to
  be on-site all day.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Commissioner Cherin seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1. Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the August 27, 2024 Malibu
  Arts Commission Regular meeting and the September 24, 2024 Malibu Arts
  Commission Regular meeting.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Appointment of Arts Commission Members to an Ad Hoe Committee for
  Conceptual Design of Parcel C
  Recommended Action: Appoint two members of the Commission to serve on an
  Ad Hoc Committee tasked with participating in the conceptual design process for
  an Arts Center on Parcel C (La Paz parcel).

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Deputy City Manager Brown stated a full
  Commission contingent was not needed to determine who would serve on the Ad
  Hoc Committee. She stated the Commission could modify the members of the Ad
  Hoc Committee in January once new Commissioners were appointed.

  Commissioners Cherin, Haldeman, and Jones expressed interest in serving on the
  Ad Hoc Committee.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Deputy City Manager Brown stated that two
  Commissioners would be allowed to serve on the Ad Hoc Committee because there
  needed to be less than a quorum.

  In response to Vice Chair Holland, Deputy City Manager Brown stated that the Ad
  Hoc Committee would discuss and recommend amenities for an Arts Center,
  including square footage. She stated that the Ad Hoc Committee would be involved
  in the conceptual process and make recommendations to the Commission.

  In response to Commissioner Cherin, Deputy City Manager Brown stated rotating
  the members of the Ad Hoc Committee would not be possible because it would
  create a daisy chain meeting that would violate the Brown Act. She stated
  Commissioners would need to be available for all Ad Hoc Committee meetings.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Deputy City Manager Brown stated City
  staff and the Ad Hoc Committee would meet with the Cross Creek Ranch
  development team. Cross Creek Ranch would put together a conceptual design for
  an Arts Center based on feedback from the Ad Hoc Committee.

  Commissioner Jones stated it was a mistake for the Commission to create a
  conceptual design without experts. He stated that a conceptual design would take a
  minimum of six months, and the Commissioners who served on the Ad Hoc
  Committee should understand the process.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Deputy City Manager Brown stated the City
  Council wanted to utilize the services readily available to create a conceptual
  design. She stated the public bidding process would be completed once the design
  was ready for construction. She stated bringing in experts could compromise their
  eligibility to assist later in the process due to potential conflicts of interest. She
  stated a public outreach process would occur to gain community feedback during
  the conceptual design process.

  Commissioner Cherin suggested appointing the Ad Hoc Committee and then
  reaffirming or modifying the Ad Hoc Committee in January.

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Commissioner Cherin seconded a motion to
  appoint Commissioners Cherin and Jones to serve on the initial Ad Hoc Committee
  tasked with participating in the conceptual design process for an Arts Center on
  Parcel C, attend meetings, and reaffirm or modify the Ad Hoc appointees in January
  2025. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Malibu Arts Commission Mid-Year Activity Report
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Malibu Arts Commission Mid—
  Year Activity Report covering the period of July through December 2024.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that the Commission would review Ad Hoc appointments in early 2025 once City
  Council appoints Commissioners. She stated Ad Hoc appointments are done yearly.

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to
  approve the Malibu Arts Commission Mid-Year Activity Report. The question was
  called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on poetry programs,
  Malibu Film Society events, and City Hall Winter Closure.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Jones stated he recently sold artwork and published his book,
  Gratitude, through Meridian Publishing.

  Commissioner Cherin stated all proceeds from Commissioner Jones's book sales
  were being donated to Malibu Urgent Care.

  Vice Chair Holland stated she resigned from the Commission effective December
  3 l , 2024. She thanked the Commissioners for their work and stated she was grateful
  to serve the community.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Arts Center Ad Hoc Committee

ADJOURNMENT

  At 10:54 a.m., Vice Chair Holland adjourned the meeting.
